statements.text: If confirmed, I envision the CDP Bureau working alongside the Office of the Special Envoy for Critical and Emerging Technology to continue to lead the Department's engagement in many international venues where artificial intelligence policy issues are discussed [...]
statements.context: Senate confirmation hearing Q&A for a State Department nominee, with written questions submitted by Senator Booker about the Bureau of Cyberspace and Digital Policy's role on AI and emerging technology.

statements.text: And so the question is, what kind of regulation? You all have spoken of that to a lot of my colleagues.
statements.context: Senator Booker questioning witnesses during a Senate Judiciary Subcommittee hearing on AI oversight, drawing an analogy to automobile regulation.

statements.text: You— Professor Marcus. I would agree. And I don't think it's a realistic thing in the world. The reason I personally signed the letter was to call attention to how serious the problems were and to emphasize spending more of our efforts on trustworthy and safe AI rather than just making a bigger version of something we already know to be unreliable.
statements.context: Spoken during a Senate Judiciary Subcommittee hearing on AI oversight, responding to Professor Gary Marcus.

statements.text: But the destructiveness that I've also seen, as a person that's seen the transformative technologies of a lot of the technologies of the last 25 years, is what really concerns me. [...] I have a lot of concerns about the corporate intention.
statements.context: Senate Judiciary Subcommittee hearing on AI oversight, Senator Booker questioning witness Professor Gary Marcus.

statements.text: The Executive Order 14110 directed Federal law enforcement agencies to produce a report on the use of AI in the criminal justice system and recommend best practices for law enforcement. [...] Can you provide the Committee with an update on the reporting requirements, including an estimate for when you expect to release the guidance on advanced law enforcement technologies in light of the fact that the deadline set in the EO has passed?
statements.context: Senate oversight hearing for the FBI, Senator Booker pressing Director Wray on a missed reporting deadline from Executive Order 14110.

statements.text: China understands if we can get two steps ahead of America on artificial intelligence, it is an endgame for them. [...] They are trying to get ahead of us in DeepSeek and AI. They are trying to get ahead of us in quantum computers. They are trying to get ahead of us in robotics.
statements.context: Senate floor speech by Senator Cory Booker responding to Senator Murphy during a debate on Trump administration policies and US-China competitiveness.
